name: Group AK executed TypeScript crosscheck (bulk key generation)
rule: Every value below was returned by a function in reference/mochimo-wots, and every input was read from group_ak_keygen_bulk.json. Nothing here is transcribed and nothing is hand-computed. Regenerate rather than edit.

oracle.why: Two implementations of one algorithm, and they can disagree. The C in reference/mochimo-core computed `addr` and `pk_sha256` in group_ak_keygen_bulk.json; the TypeScript in reference/mochimo-wots computed the values here, from the same secret, pub_seed and adrs, and neither derives from the other. This is errata 37 independence in its strong form -- the second implementation was EXECUTED, not read. It differs from group CX in two ways that are the reason it exists. First scale: CX reaches the end-to-end seed triple on seven vectors, six of them with an all-zero adrs, and seven was a fact about how many such vectors group C happened to hold rather than about what the TypeScript can be asked. This file asks every one of group AK’s thousand, half of them with a non-zero adrs, so errata 51(a)’s little-endian word-to-byte reading is corroborated by five hundred independent triples instead of by one. Second subject: CX compares the 40-byte address alone, which is ripemd160(sha3_512(pk)) duplicated into both halves, so two implementations whose 2144-byte keys differed but hashed alike would agree. Here the sha256 of the key is compared beside the address and crosscheck_matches is the conjunction, so the public key itself is the subject and not only the hash of it.
oracle.domain: Every vector in group_ak_keygen_bulk.json whose `source` begins with "wots_pkgen -> sha256 + addr_from_wots" -- the seed-triple family, which is the only one of group AK’s five the TypeScript can be asked about end to end (expand_seed, prf, thash_f and gen_chain are internals the package does not export). The selection is not trusted: the generator compares the number it selected against the header key count_wots_pkgen, written independently by the C half, and aborts when they differ. Every selected vector is then checked field by field for the shape this program consumes, so a vector nobody taught it stops the run instead of being coerced into an answer.
oracle.not_an_oracle: Group AK’s own `pk_sha256` is NOT a second opinion about the public key and is deliberately not recorded as one: the C generator produced it by calling sha256 on its own wots_pkgen output, so it and `addr` come from a single implementation and cannot disagree with each other. Nor is the sha256 executed here a third implementation of anything -- it is @noble/hashes through MochimoHasher, the same library the address hash path already uses, so it adds a comparison of the key bytes and not a second opinion about sha256 itself. And group AK’s `adrs_out_words` is not crosschecked at all: ByteBuffer.wrap COPIES (byte-buffer.ts:33-36), so the TypeScript never mutates the caller’s adrs and has no out-words to offer.
